FOREWORD This lndian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the [ndustrial Trucks Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport Engineering Division Council. In this standard the following technical changes have been incorporated: a) Normal operating conditions b) Verification procedure of truck are explained in detail;

is included; is given separately; and

c) Lateral test procedure

d) Stability test for trucks with offset loads is included, This sti]ndard was first published in 1992. The rev,ision was undertaken terrain trucks -- Stability tests' issued by the International Organization The composition of the Committee responsible to align it with ISO 8379: for Standardization. 1998 `Rough

for formulation of this standard is given at Annex A.

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revi.se~'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard ROUGH TERRAIN FORK-LIFT TRUCKS-- STABILITY TEST (First Revision)
1 SCOPE AND FIELD OF APPLICATION IS No. 11113:1999 Title Earth-moving machinery, and tractors and machinery for agriculture and forestry -- Seat index point (second revision)

1.1 This standard specifies the basic tests to verify the stability of rough terrain trucks with a rated load up to and including 10 000 kg and rough terrain variable reach trucks. 1.2 It is applicable to the above trucks:

3 TERMINOLOGY For the -purpose of this standard, the terms definitions as given in IS 4660 shall apply. 4 CONDITIONS or 4.1 Normal Operating steering Conditions The basic tests specified in this standard ensure that a rough terrain truck demonstrates satisfactory stability when reasonably and appropriately used under normal conditions, as given below: a) Nlasted trucks, stacking with the approximately vertical and the fork reasonably horizontal, on substantially smooth, level and prepared surfaces; mast arms firm, OF VALIDITY and

a) with a seated operator; b) fitted with fork arms or attachments; c) with fixed or articulated chassis; axle-locking d) which may have stabilizers, frame-levelling devices; e) with two-or four-wheel systems;

or articulated

f) with lmasts with or without tilt mechanisms; and ~) with non-s lewing booms or having slewing movement not greater than 5� either side of the longitudinal centre-plane. 1.3 It applies to rough terrain (rider-controlled) forklift trucks with a rated capacity up to and including 10000 kg, It also applies to trucks operating under the same conditions when equipped with load-handling attachments. 1.4 This standard for use as mobile loads which may four-wheel-steer g-eater than 30�. 2 REFERENCES The following standards contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below: IS No. 4660:1993 7552:2003 Title Powered industrial trucks-- Term inology (third revision) Industrial trucks operating in special condition of stacking with mast tilted forward --Additional stabi Iity tests (first revision) 1 does not apply to trucks when adapted cranes, or when handling suspended swing freely. It also does not apply to trucks with a steered wheel angle

b) Variable reach trucks, stacking with a combination of boom elevation/ extension and the fork arms reasonably horizontal, on substantially firm, smooth, level and prepared surfaces; c) Traveling with the mast or fork arms tilted rearwards and the load in the lowered (traveling) position on unimproved natural terrain and disturbed terrain areas; where applicable, any reaching/telescopic mechanism is to be fully retracted; d) Operating with the load centre of gravity approximately on the longitudinal centre plane of the truck; e) Masted trucks, manoeuvring an elevated load with the mast neither tilted r~arwards more than 10� nor the ce.ntre of gravity of the load displaced rearwards more than 600 mm; and f) Variable reach trucks, manoeuvring an elevated load with the fork arms tilted rearwards. 4.2 Operating Conditions--Other Than Normal

When the operating conditions differ from those stated in 4.1 use either: a) A truck complying with other Indian Standard(s) covering the different conditions (for example IS 7552), or

IS 13302:2003 b) Atruckwhose stability performance is agreed upon between the interested parties. This performance shall not be less than that required by the test specified for normal operating conditions in 4.1. 5 STABILITY s.1 Specification TESTS of Tests each of the truck positions, the piatform wall be tilted slowly and smoothly to the slope indicated in Table 1. The truck is considered stable, if it passes a!l the tests without overturning. For the purpose of these tests, overturning is defined as the test platform slope value which, if increased, causes overturning of the truck. 5.2.1.2 It is permissible in the lateral tests for one of the load wheels to lose contact with the test platform and it is acceptable for parts of the structure or other designed features to make contact with the test platform. 5.2.1.3 The momentum gained by a truck adopting a change in attitude is additive to that produced by the tilting platform and overturning of the truck caused by the added momentum, is to be taken as evidence of instability at that slope angle.

The stability of rough terrain trucks shall be verified by means of one of the procedures described in 5.2. 5.2 Verification 5.2.1 Procedure

Tilting Platform

5.2.1.1 A test platform which can be tilted about one side shall be used. The truck under test shall be placed on the platform, which is initially in the horizontal plane, sequentially in the positions described in Table 1. For

IS 13302:2003 5.2.2 Fised Slope 5.2.2.1 Fixed slopes, with inclinations equivalent to the prescribed test slopes, shall be used. The slope surface shall be smooth and capable of supporting the truck mass with no deformation likely to affect the test results. The truck under test shall be driven onto the fixed slopes and positioned according to Table 1. For each of the truck positions, the load shall be elevated slowly and smoothly to the height indicated in Table 1. 5.2.3 Calculation 5.2.3.1

5.3 Test Conditions 5.3. I Condi~icw of the Truck 5.3.1.1 The tests shall be carried out on an operational truck. The operator shall be represented by an object having a mass of 90 kg if the stability during a test is thereby decreased. The centre of gravity of the object shall be secured 150 mm above the seat index point (SIP), as determined in accordance withIS11113, with the seat at mid-point of the adjustments provided. Fuel tanks of engined trucks shall be full, if stability is thereby reduced; all other tanks shall be filled to their correct operating levels. Tyres shall be inflated to their correct pressure specified by the truck manufacturer. Where tyre ballast is incorporated in the truck design, the use of ballast shall be in accordance with the truck manufacturer's instructions. 5.3.2 Position of the Truck on the Platform 5.3.2.1 For Tests 1 and 2 (~ee Table 1),,the truck shall be placed on the test platform so that the load axle is parallel to the tilt axis, Al', of the test platform [see Fig I(c), 2(d) and 2(e)]. Stabilizers or axle locking may only be used for Tests 1 and 3. For Tests 3,4 and 5 (see Table l). The truck shall be positioned on the test platform in a turning position with line MN parallel to the tilt axis, XY, of the test platform [see Figs. 2(c) to 2(0]. Trucks positioned as shown in Figs. 2(c), (d), (~ and (g) shall have the steer wheel nearest to the tilt axis parallel with the tilt axis. 5.3.2.2 Lateral stability tests shall be conducted to the side of the truck which is the least stable. Point Nis the centre point of the area of contact between the test platform surface and the front wheel or the stabilizer contact pad nearest the tilting axis [see Figs. 2(c) to 2(g)]. s,3.2.3 Point M is defined as follows:

5.3.3.1 The test load shall be a mass equivalent to the maximum load Q, as indicated on.the information plate of the truck, which the truck can elevate to its maximum lift height acting through the centre of gravity, G, nominally positioned at the standard load centre distance, D, both horizontally from the front face of the fork arm shank and vertically from the upper face of the fork arm blade (see Fig. 3 and Table 2). 5.3.3.2 When additional lift heights, loads and load centre distances are to be indicated on the information plate, the truck shall meet the requirements established by the tests specified in this standard for these additional ratings. 5.3.3.3 The centre of gravity, G, of the test load (see Fig. 3) shall be located in the longitudinal centre plane, AB, of the truck [see Figs. 1(c), 1(d) and 1(e), and 6(c) and 6(d)]. 5.3.4 Location of the Truck on the Platform 5.3.4.1 The truck shall be positioned in accordance with table of tests (see Table 1). The initial position of the truck on the test platform shall be maintained during each test. This may be achieved by application of the parking or service brakes, which maybe secured in the `on' position, or by wedging the wheels against the truck frame, ensuring however that articulation is not affected. Blocks (chocks) having a maximum height not exceeding the value indicated in Table 3 may be used, if necessary, to maintain the initial position of the truck on the te-st platform. Block (chocks), if used, shall not artificially improve stability. Stabilizers or axle 3

5.3.7 Lift Height for Tests Simulating

Travel

For tests simulating travel, that is, Tests 2 and 4, the upper face of the fork arms, measured at the heels of the fork arms when fully tilted rearward, shall be positioned approximately 500 mm from the test platform [see Fig. 5(a) 5(b), 6(a) and 6(b)]. 5.3.8 Lateral Test Procedure Lateral tests shall be conducted to the side to which the truck is least stable. For trucks with operator-selectable stabilizers, or axle locking, Test 3 shall be conducted both with stabilizers and axle lock engaged and disengaged. For trucks fitted with operator-selectable stabilizers of chassis level ling, test 3 may be performed with a maximum of 7 percent (4�) of lateral correction [see Fig. 2(a), 2(b) and 2(t)]. 5.3.9 Lateral Stacking Test (Unladen)

dwi[htnasts

Test I shall be conducted with the horizontal position ofa load datum point, E, unchanged when elevated from its lowered position [see Fig4(c)]. By means of a plumb line or other suitable equipment, set the mast vertical, elevate the fork and the specified test load to approximately 500 mm above the test platform. With the front face of the fork arm shank vertical, establish a point E [see Fig. 4(a)] on the fork or fork carrier, having a fixed relationship to the centre of gravity of the test load G (see Fig 3). Point E shall be used to provide a reference datum F on the test platform [(see Fig. 4(a)]. When the mast is elevated, a new point F] on the test platform may occur [see Fig. 4(b)]. By the following adjustments, this new point FI can be returned to the original location of F [see Fig,. 4(c)], as follows: a) For trucks with tiltable masts, changes in the location of FI shall be corrected by varying the tilt of the mast within the limits provided by the desig,n of the truck. b) For trucks with fixed masts, adjustments in the fork arms or fork carrier tilt (where provided) may be used to correct for changes in location of point F1 within the limits of tilt provided by the design of the truck. c) For truck having non-tiltab]e masts, fork arms, or fork carrier, adjustments cannot be made. 5.3.5.2 Trucks with variable reach mechanism

5.3.9.1 The unladen lateral stacking tests for roasted trucks shall be conducted at maximum backward tilt. For variable reach trucks, tests shall be conducted at maximum and minimum boom extension, at maximum boom angle. 5.3.10 Safety Precautions 5.3.10.1 Precautions shall be taken to prevent the overturning of the truck or displacement of the test load during the course of the test. If the means for preventing the total overturning of the truck consist of rope lashing or chain, this shall be sufficiently slack to impose no appreciable restriction on the truck until the overturning is reached. 5.3.10.2 Displacement of the test load shall prevented by means such as: be

a) firmly securing the test load to the carrier or equivalent structure; b) suspending the test load near the ground from an approp~ate support placed on th= fork so that the suspension point is at the point where the centre of gravity G (Fig. 3) of the test load would be if the test load were to be place on the fork. 6 STABILITY TESTS ATTACHMENTS FOR TRUCKS WITH

Tests I and 3 shall be conducted with the load in the least stable combination of lift and reach, as determined by the manufacturer [see Fig. I(b) and 2(b)]. 5.3.6 Trucks with Selectable Locking Stabilizers anaYor Axle

Tests 1 and 3 shall be conducted both with stabilizers engaged and disengaged [see Fig. 1(f) and 2(fi]. 4

Trucks fitted with attachments shall be subjected to the same stability tests, except where the attachment can bring the centre of gravity of the load out of the longitudinal centre plane AB of the truck [see Fig. 1(c), 1(d) and 1(e)] (see 7 for this case). For verification of the vertical position of the mast, a reference point having a fixed relationship to the centre of gravity of the test load G (see Fig. 3) shall be chosen. The test load shall be the nominal load at the nominal centre distance specified for the attachment when used on the truck being tested. The lift heights required in the tests shall be measured between the surface of the tilting
